Re-derived from public ChEMBL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Every value traces to a recorded database release. This one IS reproducible — re-running the rule against ChEMBL_37 reproduces it.

active_snapshot_facts.join_is_lossless: All four columns are a pure function of the axis string — across the 39 axes appearing on both nerve sides, zero disagreement. So 144 axis-keyed rows populate all 183 table rows exactly.

column_semantics.tier_v2: Axis tier = best (lowest-ordinal) tier among constituent genes, ordered {'1_':1,'1b':1.5,'2_':2,'3_':3,'4_':4}. Genes come from splitting the axis on '|' then each end on '_' to expand LIANA subunit complexes.
column_semantics.agents_flagged: 'GENE: AGENT [tag]; ...' joined by ' | '. '[WITHDRAWN]' takes precedence over '[black-box]'. '[clinical]' marks a gene with no approved agent.
column_semantics.glioma_trials: '<agent> (<n>: <first three NCT ids>)' joined by ' | '. A truncated summary, not the full trial list.
column_semantics.withdrawn: Per-gene market-withdrawn approved agents, 'GENE: AGENT; AGENT' joined by ' | '. Populated on 13 axes covering BENZIODARONE, PRENYLAMINE, PROBUCOL.

adoption_2026-08-19.rationale: Every value now traces to a recorded database release (ChEMBL_37) rather than partly to a prior-session artifact nobody can inspect. Accepted with its cost stated below.
adoption_2026-08-19.cost_accepted: 12 of 183 table rows leave 1_approved_available, concentrated in the ITGB1 and CALM/PDE1 axes, whose tier-1 status rested on agents supplied by the permanently lost prior-pass artifact rather than by ChEMBL.
adoption_2026-08-19.gain: 18 rows leave 4_no_chembl_target because exact gene-symbol resolution finds targets the original full-text search missed.

impact_on_the_183_row_table.geometry_untouched: ranks, magnitudes, row counts, interfaces, immune, nerve_side, compartment_side and min_pval are all bit-identical — adoption swaps only the drug annotation
impact_on_the_183_row_table.withdrawn_rows_changed: 0/183 — the re-queried column agrees exactly with the tag-derived one, so adoption does not disturb it

adoption_2026-08-19.notable_correction: CALM1|PDE1A and CALM1|PDE1C move 1_approved_available -> 1b_approved_withdrawn_only. That is a correction, not a loss: they are the 'CALM1 axes are a trap' cases, where the only approved agents on the CALM1 end (benziodarone, prenylamine) are market-withdrawn.
adoption_2026-08-19.cross_validation: The `withdrawn` column re-queried directly from ChEMBL's withdrawn_flag matches the column derived independently by rule derive_withdrawn_agents from the inline [WITHDRAWN] tags on 13/13 axes, character for character. Two derivations sharing no code and no data path, agreeing exactly.

limits_that_still_apply: GLIOMA-TRIAL COVERAGE IS BOUNDED BY A HAND-CURATED 20-AGENT LIST (curated_agent_map_2026-08-07.json). An empty glioma_trials cell means no NAMED trial for a LISTED agent — not that no trial exists.
CLINICALTRIALS.GOV HAS NO RELEASE VERSION. Only the retrieval date pins it; trial counts drift continuously.
TIERS ARE PHARMACOLOGICAL REACHABILITY, NOT BIOLOGICAL IMPORTANCE. 4_no_chembl_target means no database record, which is often a statement about drug-discovery attention rather than about the target.

unreproducible_original.applies_to: nerve_immune_axis_drug_annotation_2026-08-07.csv only — the active snapshot IS reproducible
reasons: ChEMBL release was never recorded, so even an identical re-query cannot be proven equivalent.

One input is permanently lost: genes with no ChEMBL mechanism record inherited approved/clinical agents from a prior-session artifact addressed only as UUID 34d720d0-5c16-46bb-92e6-d8d6b6a02ec3 (evidence_source == 'prior_reference_pass'). Not in this repo, not recoverable.
The generator's handoff/*.json MCP response caches did not survive the session.

refreshing.naming: Refreshed snapshots are nerve_immune_axis_drug_annotation_refreshed_<DATE>.csv. The `_refreshed_` infix keeps the rule's date wildcard namespace disjoint from committed pinned/derived snapshots, so it can never resolve to one and shadow it.
refreshing.behaviour: Opt-in, never in `rule all`. Writes a NEW dated file plus refresh_manifest_<DATE>.json; never overwrites an existing snapshot.
refreshing.adoption: Bump config.lead_axes.drug_annotation deliberately, after diffing. Not automatic — drift is a scientific judgement, not a build step.
refreshing.failure_semantics: Aborts with [FAIR-ALERT] and writes no output rather than emitting a partial snapshot. An unresolved gene would silently become '4_no_chembl_target', which reads downstream as 'this target has no chemistry' — a scientific claim manufactured by a network error. Verified under real failure: a run aborted on gene C3 after 4 backed-off retries and wrote nothing.
refreshing.records_chembl_release: Yes — read from /status and required. The rule refuses to mint an unpinned snapshot.

sources.chembl: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data — /target filtered on target_components__target_component_synonyms__component_synonym__iexact (NOT /target/search, which rejects target_type/organism filters with a 400 and 400s outright on short symbols like C3), then /mechanism, then /molecule/{id} per molecule. No API key.
sources.clinicaltrials: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies — query.cond + query.intr (NOT query.intv). No API key.

gotchas_found_by_running_it: ChEMBL_37 serialises max_phase as the STRING '4.0'. A naive `phase == 4` is always False, so every approved drug silently falls through to 3_chembl_target_no_agent. The first successful run produced a clean-looking 144-axis snapshot claiming ZERO approved or clinical agents across all 156 genes, exit code 0, no error. A plausibility guard now refuses to write any snapshot where no axis reaches an approved or clinical tier.

/target/search cannot be used for gene-symbol resolution. The exact synonym filter is also more precise: exactly one human target per gene rather than a fuzzy ranked list, so a near-miss cannot be mistaken for a hit.
